text:
alex: FYI — customer reported our auto-tool selector invoked payments.capture instead of refunds.create and ended up charging the account. attaching payload/logs, cc @maria @ryan @ingrid

alex: request body they sent:
```json
POST /v1/invoke
{
  "user_id": "acct_123",
  "input": "refund order 12345 for $59.99",
  "tool_hint": "refund",
  "candidates": ["payments.capture", "refunds.create", "ledger.apply_credit"]
}
```

alex: service response we see in logs:
```json
{
  "tool": "payments.capture",
  "status": "invoked",
  "args": { "amount": "59.99" },
  "result": "charge_succeeded"
}
```

maria: ouch. Does selector do fuzzy substring matching? :eyes:

ryan: looks like the resolver favored the first candidate that matched token "pay" vs "refund" because of a heuristic. reproducing locally now. initial hypothesis: namespace-rank weight bug + permissive arg coercion (string->number) allowed payments.capture to accept amount.

ingrid: support-bot created SL-5124 and auto-assigned to eng-oncall. customer escalated, wants reversal and root cause. billing-bot: please create manual refund if needed.

billing-bot: manual reversal created INV-9876 (pending). tagging customer for confirmation.

oncall: I'm on it — will reproduce with the exact candidates list and our selector config. expected timeline: 1-2h for repro, then hotfix.

ryan: repro steps: curl below reproduces the wrong resolver pick in latest staging.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -d '{"input":"refund 59.99","tool_hint":"refund","candidates":["payments.capture","refunds.create","ledger.apply_credit"]}'
```

ryan: stack trace shows resolver.allowed_matchers includes substring fallback; patch will narrow to exact namespace match + require candidate namespace to match tool_hint stem.

maria: also add schema strictness: refunds.create schema requires amount:number and currency:string; payments.capture currently accepts amount:string which caused silent cast. tighten validation.

alex: please include test that simulates ambiguous candidate ordering and ensures refunds.create wins when hint contains "refund".

ryan: ack. I'm opening PR now for two changes: (1) resolver matching priority fix, (2) stricter schema validation on calling layer. PR #2436. will canary to 5% then 25%.

ingrid: customer asked for timeline — can we offer reversal ETA? billing-bot will do manual reversal asap and confirm.

billing-bot: manual refund issued to customer; email sent.

maria: note for postmortem: ambiguous tool names and permissive coercion = failure mode. add to incidents backlog.

support-bot: escalation SL-5124 status updated: assigned->in_progress, owner: ryan.

ryan: deployed patch to canary (5%). monitoring logs for misrouted invocation. added extra logging to resolver decisions and candidate scores.

alex: good. please post canary metrics here after 1h. also include sample logs showing resolver score for that request id when you have it. :thumbsup:

ryan: after 35m canary metrics: 0/3 misroutes, resolver logs show refunds.create score 0.92 vs payments.capture 0.67 when hint="refund" — before patch it was flipped.

ingrid: customer confirmed refund received, closing the billing impact.

maria: once PR merged, please add a tiny migration note for private deployments that pin an older resolver policy.

ryan: PR merged, rollout to 100% at +30m. adding unit tests and an e2e in ci. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2436

alex: thanks all. follow-up actions: (1) incidents postmortem (ingrid), (2) add candidate disambiguation docs (maria), (3) add regression alert for schema coercion (ryan). closing thread when postmortem linked. :pray:
